## What The Business Is
QUALCOMM INC (QCOM) is a semiconductor and wireless-technology company best known for Snapdragon chipsets and cellular intellectual property. It operates primarily through **QCT**, which sells chips and platforms for handsets, automotive, IoT, PCs, edge AI and emerging data-center products, and **QTL**, which licenses Qualcomm’s wireless patent portfolio. In its fiscal Q2 2026 call, management framed Qualcomm as a “connected edge to data center” AI compute company, not only a smartphone supplier.

## What It Does
Qualcomm designs system-on-chips, modems, RF front-end, connectivity, AI accelerators, CPUs and software platforms used in smartphones, vehicles, PCs, wearables, industrial devices and networks. Its Snapdragon Digital Chassis targets cockpit, telematics, ADAS and automated-driving workloads; Snapdragon X targets AI PCs; industrial/robotics platforms target edge and “physical AI”; and the new Dragonfly portfolio targets data-center CPUs, inference accelerators, connectivity and custom silicon. At Investor Day 2026, Qualcomm said its Dragonfly data-center roadmap includes the C1000 CPU, High Bandwidth Compute, AI300 inference accelerator and custom silicon solutions. ([qualcomm.com](https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/2026/06/qualcomm-unveils-comprehensive-data-center-roadmap-for-the-agent?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)
Fiscal Q2 2026 results were solid versus guidance: Qualcomm reported **$10.6 billion** revenue and **$2.65 non-GAAP EPS**, with QCT revenue of **$9.1 billion** and QTL revenue of **$1.4 billion**; it also returned **$3.7 billion** to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. Automotive remained a standout: QCT Automotive revenue was **$1.3 billion**, up **38% year over year**, and management said automotive annualized revenue exceeded **$5 billion** for the first time, with an expected fiscal 2026 exit run-rate above **$6 billion**. ([s204.q4cdn.com](https://s204.q4cdn.com/645488518/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/FY2026-2nd-Quarter-Earnings-Release.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The biggest recent strategic development was the June 24 Investor Day, where Qualcomm raised its fiscal 2029 **non-handset revenue target to $40 billion**, including **more than $15 billion** from data-center AI infrastructure and **$10 billion** from automotive; it also expanded its automotive design-win pipeline to **$65 billion** and targeted **more than $18 non-GAAP EPS** in fiscal 2029. ([investor.qualcomm.com](https://investor.qualcomm.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Qualcomm-Accelerates-Diversification-with-Comprehensive-Strategy-for-Data-Center-and-Sees-Multiple-Inflection-Points-Over-the-Next-3-to-5-Years/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Qualcomm also announced a **multi-year, multi-generation agreement with Meta** to supply data-center CPUs, giving more concrete customer validation to its data-center ambitions. The company said the Dragonfly roadmap is optimized for agentic AI inference with emphasis on performance per watt, token throughput and lower total cost of ownership. ([qualcomm.com](https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/2026/06/qualcomm-unveils-comprehensive-data-center-roadmap-for-the-agent?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)
Near-term handset weakness remains the main overhang. On the fiscal Q2 call, management said China Android QCT shipments were “meaningfully below” end-consumer demand because handset OEMs were reducing build plans and drawing down channel inventory amid memory supply and pricing pressures. Qualcomm guided fiscal Q3 revenue to **$9.2 billion–$10.0 billion** and non-GAAP EPS to **$2.10–$2.30**, with QCT handset revenue expected around **$4.9 billion**, down sequentially. ([s204.q4cdn.com](https://s204.q4cdn.com/645488518/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/FY2026-2nd-Quarter-Earnings-Release.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The diversification story is promising but execution-heavy. Data center pits Qualcomm against entrenched AI infrastructure suppliers and hyperscaler in-house silicon programs; its new Investor Day targets are forward-looking and depend on successful product ramps, software ecosystem adoption, customer wins and manufacturing execution. Qualcomm’s own Investor Day release emphasized that targets and diversification initiatives are subject to risks and uncertainties. ([investor.qualcomm.com](https://investor.qualcomm.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Qualcomm-Accelerates-Diversification-with-Comprehensive-Strategy-for-Data-Center-and-Sees-Multiple-Inflection-Points-Over-the-Next-3-to-5-Years/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

China exposure and export constraints add risk. Recent reporting said Qualcomm plans China-compliant versions of Dragonfly data-center products, but that strategy must navigate U.S. export thresholds and a changing regulatory environment. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/qualcomm-plans-china-specific-data-center-chips-built-to-clear-us-export-limits?utm_source=openai))

## Bull Case
Qualcomm is transitioning from a smartphone-cyclical to a diversified "edge-to-data-center" AI compute company. The June 2026 Investor Day raised the FY29 non-handset target to $40B (>$15B data center, $10B auto), backed by a concrete multi-year Meta CPU agreement, a $65B automotive design-win pipeline (auto revenue +38% y/y, exiting FY26 above $6B run-rate), and Snapdragon X2 PC momentum. QTL is softening on low-tier units. The data-center story is execution-heavy against NVIDIA, AMD, ARM-server incumbents and hyperscaler in-house silicon; targets are 3–5 years out and the Investor Day pop may already be largely priced. Ramping data-center R&D and capex will pressure FCF in the interim. China exposure (~large share of QCT) and U.S. export rules add regulatory tail risk. **Forward FCF estimate: $13,000M.** TTM FCF is $12,516M. Near-term Q3 weakness (revenue $9.2–10.0B guidance, handset decline to $4.9B) will pressure the front half of the 12-month window. Full-year revenue likely grows to ~$46–47B, but near-term margin compression from handset mix shift and ramp costs tempers FCF conversion. Net result: modest FCF growth to ~$13.0B, below the revenue growth rate, reflecting transitional capex and mix headwinds during the ramp.

**EV → Market Cap bridge:** Current EV–MC gap is $9,835.0M ($202,685.4M – $192,850.4M), representing net debt. Qualcomm generates strong FCF and returns significant capital ($3.7B in Q2 alone), but also carries meaningful debt and is entering an investment cycle for data-center R&D and custom-silicon programs. I hold the gap approximately constant at $9,835M — capital returns funded by FCF are roughly offset by continued debt service and any incremental capex-related financing.

**Forward EV:** $13,000M × 18.0x = $234,000M

**Forward Market Cap:** $234,000M – $9,835M = $224,165M

The multiple expansion from 16.2x to 18.0x is moderate and reflects a market that is beginning to price Qualcomm as a diversified AI-compute franchise rather than a handset cyclical. I do not go higher than 18x because: (1) much of the Investor Day narrative is fresh and partially priced; (2) data-center revenue is still de minimis in the 12-month window — initial shipments ≠ meaningful revenue; (3) competitive intensity in data-center AI is extreme; and (4) handset cyclicality and Apple share loss keep a floor under the risk premium. The expansion is supported by the fact that automotive is delivering revenue now (not promises), the handset business is at a cyclical trough (limiting downside), and the second derivative on diversification is positive.

## Bull Case
Qualcomm's diversification thesis is gaining concrete traction. Automotive revenue hit $1.3B in fiscal Q2 (up 38% y/y) with a $65B design-win pipeline and a fiscal 2026 exit run-rate above $6B. The Meta multi-year data-center CPU agreement and Dragonfly roadmap (C1000, AI300, custom silicon) provide credible customer validation for a genuinely new growth vector, with initial hyperscaler shipments in the December quarter. Snapdragon X2 outperforming Intel by 30% positions Qualcomm to capture PC share. China handset shipments are expected to bottom in Q3 and return to growth, meaning the worst near-term headwind is likely behind us. The $40B fiscal 2029 non-handset revenue target and $18+ EPS guide show management's confidence in durable diversification.

## Bear Case
Near-term fundamentals are deteriorating: Q3 guidance of $9.2-10.0B revenue and $2.10-2.30 EPS is a sharp step-down from Q2's $10.6B/$2.65. Handset revenue declining to ~$4.9B from $6B reflects OEM destocking and memory pricing pressures. The Apple modem share step-down in the September quarter will further pressure QCT handset revenue. Data-center targets are fiscal 2029 — extremely far out — and pit Qualcomm against entrenched incumbents (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom) and hyperscaler in-house silicon. The Investor Day on June 24 likely front-loaded much of the re-rating optimism. China export-control risk adds uncertainty to both handset and data-center revenue. Near-term margin compression is real.

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple:** 16.2x EV/FCF (202,685 / 12,516)
- **12-month forward multiple:** 17.0x
- **Direction:** EXPAND
- **Drivers:**
  1. **Data-center revenue inflection:** Initial Dragonfly/hyperscaler shipments in the December quarter will convert the narrative from promise to realized revenue, supporting multiple expansion even as near-term handset FCF is depressed (the optical multiple should rise as capex/ramp costs compress near-term FCF while the growth optionality becomes tangible).
  2. **Automotive growth durability with positive second derivative:** Auto revenue growing 38% y/y with an expanding $65B pipeline and exit run-rate above $6B demonstrates this is not a one-off; the acceleration itself justifies a higher multiple on the diversified earnings base.
  3. **China handset bottoming:** If Q3 proves to be the trough as management expects, the removal of the primary bear-case overhang should release multiple compression that has weighed on the stock. Rates appear stable-to-easing, supporting duration-sensitive growth multiples.

The expansion is modest (not aggressive) because the June 24 Investor Day already partially priced the long-term vision. However, the market has not yet seen actual data-center revenue, and the gap between narrative and numbers is where the next leg of re-rating lives.

## Logic
**Forward FCF estimate: $12,800M.** TTM FCF is $12,516M, up 6.9% y/y. Over the next 12 months, near-term handset weakness and the Apple share step-down will pressure QCT handset FCF, but automotive growth (50% y/y expected in Q3), IoT strength, and initial data-center shipments should partially offset. Net income may dip near-term given Q3 guidance, but FCF should hold reasonably well given Qualcomm's licensing cash flows (QTL) and capital-efficiency in the diversification businesses. I estimate modest ~2.3% FCF growth to ~$12,800M, reflecting the tug-of-war between transitory handset headwinds and durable diversification growth.

**Applied multiple: 17.0x EV/FCF.** This is a modest expansion from 16.2x, reflecting early-stage data-center revenue realization, durable automotive acceleration, and the expected clearing of the China handset overhang — but tempered by the fact that Investor Day optimism is already partially in the price and execution risk on fiscal 2029 targets remains high.

**EV to market cap bridge:** Current EV minus market-cap gap = $202,685.4M - $192,850.4M = $9,835M (net cash). Qualcomm has been returning capital ($3.7B in Q2) but also generating FCF, so the net cash position should be roughly stable. Forward market cap = (17.0 × $12,800) - $9,835 = $217,600 - $9,835 = **$207,765M**.
